name: Sanagala Basavanna
location: In front of Lord Shiva sanctum
significance: Prime devotee and vehicle Nandi representing Dharma; head of all Ganas whose consent is mandatory before worshipping Lord Shiva.

name: Ratnagarbha Ganapathi (Chintamani Ganapathi)
significance: Exclusive Chintamani avatar brought by Shiva-Parvathi; worshipped with 440 mantras to eliminate troubles.

name: Sudarshana Veerabhadra Swamy
significance: First protector deity greeting devotees; swallowed Sudarshan Chakra during Daksha Yagna destruction.

name: Jwala Veerabhadra Swamy
location: Facing North, to the left of 5 Pandava Lingas
significance: 10-armed idol with regional depiction wearing skull garland, created from Shiva's matted locks.

name: Kumara Swamy Shrine
significance: 6-faced, 12-armed deity balancing 6 enemies of mind; dearest son of Shiva-Parvati who inspired their move to Srisailam.

name: Uma Maheswara Swamy Temple
significance: Depicts Ardhanarishwara Tattva with Shiva seated on throne holding Uma on left thigh; site of Parvati's penance.

name: Vruddha Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
location: Facing North to main Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
significance: Ancient temple with decorated inner walls and Dvarabhandhams featuring Gajalakshmi, Lion, and guardians.

name: Rama Prathistitha Sahasra Lingam
significance: Sahasralingam established by Lord Rama to cleanse Brahmahatyadosham after slaying Ravana.

name: Seetha Prathistitha Sahasra Lingam
significance: Sahasralingam consecrated by Sita Devi alongside Lord Rama.

name: Raja Rajeswara & Raja Rajeshwari Temple
location: Northeast of Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple, facing West
significance: Oldest temple complex inside sanctum; Gaja Lakshmi Devi and 4-armed Rajarajeshwari seated on throne.

name: Ardhanareeswara Temple
location: North of Mallikarjuna Temple, facing East
significance: Seated idol in Lotus Pose depicting combined form of Shiva and Parvati with Lion vehicle.

name: Saptamatrikalu Shrine
significance: 7 divine mothers (Brahmani, Maheshwari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Indrani, Chamundi) who stopped Andhakasura's blood.

name: Lopamudradevi Shrine
significance: Dedicated to Agastya's wife Lopamudra, primary worshipper of Haadividya and Srividya.

name: Pancha (Pandava) Lingalu
location: Courtyard of Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
significance: 5 Lingas established individually by Yudhishtara, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva.

name: Nagula Katta
significance: Subramanya Swamy worshipped in serpent form across 8 serpent demigods to eradicate Nagadosha and Kujadosha.

name: Triphala Vruksham
significance: Combined Medi (Brahma), Raavi (Vishnu), Juvvi (Shiva) tree where Dattatreya & Nrusimha Saraswathi performed Tapasya.

name: Tella Maddi Vruksham
significance: Sacred Arjuna tree representing manifestation of Lord Shiva, Vishnu, and Ganesha.

name: Sami (Jammi) Vruksham
significance: Aparajita Devi in disguise; hiding spot of Pandava weapons worshipped on Vijayadashami.

name: Sri Gokulam (Go Pooja & Gosala)
significance: Houses over 1500 cows providing milk for Abhishekams and Panchagavya by-products.

name: Jagadguru Panditharadhya Peetham
significance: Surya Simhasana Peetham of Veera Saivam tradition led by Dr. Channa Siddharama Panditharadhya Sivacharyulu.

name: Shivaji Khadgam Sculpture
significance: Sculpture depicting Chatrapathi Shivaji Maharaj receiving the divine sword from Bhramarambika Devi.

name: Chandravathi Sculpture
significance: Depicts Princess Chandravathi offering jasmine garland to Lord Shiva.

name: Manjari Sculpture
significance: Depicts devotee Manjari in eternal prayer near Garbhalaya.
